questions.q: How many players from one team are on the pitch in football?
questions.e: Each side plays with eleven players.

questions.q: Which coloured card sends a player off the pitch?
questions.e: A red card means the player must leave.

questions.q: Who is known as "CR7"?
questions.e: CR7 stands for Cristiano Ronaldo and his shirt number.

questions.q: Which country won the 2022 FIFA World Cup?
questions.e: Argentina beat France on penalties in the final.

questions.q: Which country has won the most men's World Cups?
questions.e: Brazil has won the World Cup five times.

questions.q: Which English club went unbeaten in the 2003-04 Premier League season?
questions.e: Arsenal's team was nicknamed "The Invincibles".

questions.q: Who scored the famous "Hand of God" goal in 1986?
questions.e: Maradona scored it against England at the 1986 World Cup.

questions.q: Which club did Lionel Messi leave in 2021 after joining as a teenager?
questions.e: Messi spent his early career at Barcelona.

questions.q: Which country hosted the 2018 FIFA World Cup?
questions.e: Russia hosted the tournament in 2018.

questions.q: How many Ballon d'Or awards has Lionel Messi won?
questions.e: Messi has won the Ballon d'Or eight times.

questions.q: Who scored a record 36 goals in a Premier League season in 2022-23?
questions.e: Haaland set the 38-game season record.

questions.q: Which club has won the most European Cup / Champions League titles?
questions.e: Real Madrid has the most titles by a distance.

questions.q: What is the nickname of Nigeria's women's national football team?
questions.e: The Super Falcons are Nigeria's women's team.

questions.q: What is the nickname of Nigeria's men's national basketball team?
questions.e: The team is known as D'Tigers.

questions.q: How many times have the Super Eagles won the Africa Cup of Nations?
questions.e: Nigeria won in 1980, 1994 and 2013.

questions.q: In which year did Nigeria win Olympic football gold?
questions.e: Nigeria won gold at the Atlanta Olympics in 1996.

questions.q: Which Nigerian-born basketball legend starred for the Houston Rockets?
questions.e: Hakeem "The Dream" Olajuwon was born in Lagos.

questions.q: Who scored Nigeria's first-ever World Cup goal, at the 1994 tournament?
questions.e: Rashidi Yekini scored against Bulgaria in 1994.

questions.q: Who won Nigeria's first individual Olympic gold medal, in the long jump in 1996?
questions.e: Chioma Ajunwa won gold in Atlanta.

questions.q: Jay-Jay Okocha played in England for which club?
questions.e: Okocha became a Bolton legend.

questions.q: Which Nigerian striker was named CAF African Player of the Year in 2023?
questions.e: Osimhen won the CAF award in 2023.

questions.q: How many players from one team are on a basketball court?
questions.e: Each side has five players on court.

questions.q: How many points is a shot from behind the arc worth?
questions.e: A three-point shot is worth three points.

questions.q: With which team did Michael Jordan win six NBA titles?
questions.e: Jordan led the Bulls to six championships.

questions.q: How high is a basketball hoop above the floor?
questions.e: The rim is 10 feet high.

questions.q: On which surface is Wimbledon played?
questions.e: Wimbledon is the famous grass-court Grand Slam.

questions.q: How many Grand Slam tournaments are held each year?
questions.e: The four are the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon and US Open.

questions.q: Which Grand Slam is played on clay?
questions.e: The French Open is played at Roland Garros.

questions.q: Which player won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, the most in the Open Era?
questions.e: Serena Williams won 23 major singles titles.

questions.q: Who won the French Open a record 14 times?
questions.e: Nadal is known as the King of Clay.

questions.q: How many rings are on the Olympic flag?
questions.e: The five rings represent the continents.

questions.q: Who holds the men's 100m world record of 9.58 seconds?
questions.e: Bolt set it in Berlin in 2009.

questions.q: How long is a marathon?
questions.e: A marathon is 26.2 miles, or 42.195 km.

questions.q: How often are the Summer Olympic Games held?
questions.e: The Summer Games take place every four years.

questions.q: Which boxer said "Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee"?
questions.e: The line belongs to Muhammad Ali.

questions.q: In which city did Anthony Joshua win Olympic gold in 2012?
questions.e: Joshua won super-heavyweight gold at London 2012.

questions.q: Who became the youngest heavyweight world champion, aged 20, in 1986?
questions.e: Mike Tyson won the title in November 1986.

questions.q: The 1974 "Rumble in the Jungle" between Ali and Foreman was held in which country (then called Zaire)?
questions.e: The fight took place in Kinshasa.

questions.q: Which Nigerian boxer was world middleweight champion in the early 1960s?
questions.e: Dick Tiger (Richard Ihetu) won the middleweight title in 1962.

questions.q: A football match has two halves of 45 minutes.
questions.e: Normal time is 90 minutes in two halves.

questions.q: A basketball team has seven players on the court.
questions.e: Only five players per team are on court.

questions.q: Wimbledon is played on clay courts.
questions.e: Wimbledon is played on grass.

questions.q: Nigeria has won the men's FIFA World Cup.
questions.e: Nigeria has played at several World Cups but has not won it.

questions.q: Usain Bolt is from Jamaica.
questions.e: Usain Bolt is a Jamaican sprinter.

questions.q: A marathon is longer than 40 kilometres.
questions.e: A marathon is 42.195 km.

questions.q: A goalkeeper may pick up the ball with their hands inside their own penalty area.
questions.e: Goalkeepers can handle the ball inside their penalty area.
